subject: Hospitality
title: Adaptive Reuse: Old Buildings, New Hotels
description: A micro-lesson that makes Adaptive Reuse: Old Buildings, New Hotels usable.

hook.text: A former prison in Boston became the Liberty Hotel. A Dutch crane turned into a penthouse suite.

buildup.text: Converting existing buildings into hotels preserves character, reduces construction waste.

discovery.text: Factories, churches, banks, courthouses, and even water towers have been transformed into boutique hotels worldwide.

twist.text: Adaptive reuse is often more expensive than new construction. Old buildings have structural surprises, code compliance costs.

climax.text: But the premium pays off: guests pay more for a hotel with a story. 'You're sleeping in a 200-year-old bank vault' is.

punchline.text: Prisons, churches, cranes. Old buildings make the most memorable hotels.

quiz.question: Why is adaptive reuse popular despite higher costs?
options: It creates unique properties with stories that guests pay premium prices for
